items.title: The Crystal Palace
items.description: A landmark of industrial architecture built for London's Great Exhibition. Constructed from cast iron and plate glass, it demonstrated early modular prefabrication on a massive scale.

items.title: Metropolis Film Poster
items.description: An iconic Art Deco graphic design masterpiece featuring towering geometric skyscrapers and a streamlined metallic robot. It defined sci-fi visual language for a century.

items.title: The 'New Look' Bar Suit
items.description: Revolutionized post-war fashion by rejecting wartime fabric rationing with cinched waists and voluminous pleated skirts. It re-established Paris as the global capital of haute couture.

items.title: Eames Lounge Chair & Ottoman
items.description: Designed for the Herman Miller furniture company, this piece elevated molded plywood and soft leather into a mid-century luxury staple designed to mimic the feel of a well-worn baseball glove.

items.title: Valentine Typewriter
items.description: Created for Olivetti, this bright red portable typewriter turned a drab office machine into an anti-academic pop culture fashion statement precursor to modern industrial consumer design.

items.title: Wassily Chair (Model B3)
items.description: Designed while Marcel Breuer was leading the Bauhaus woodwork shop, this landmark piece was inspired by the bent tubular steel of bicycle handlebars. By replacing traditional bulky upholstery with taut leather straps, Breuer stripped the armchair down to its essential geometric form.

items.title: Fallingwater
items.description: Built over a natural waterfall in rural Pennsylvania, Fallingwater is Frank Lloyd Wright's ultimate expression of organic architecture. Cantilevered concrete terraces project dramatically over the stream, seamlessly integrating human living space with the surrounding forest.

items.title: Farnsworth House
items.description: Designed as a weekend retreat, this steel-and-glass residence embodies Mies van der Rohe's minimalist dictum 'less is more.' Elevated above a floodplain on white steel columns, its transparent floor-to-ceiling glass walls blur the line between nature and living quarters.

contexts.title: WWI
contexts.description: The First World War shattered European empires and traditional ideals, triggering existential trauma that catalyzed radical art movements like Dada, Futurism, and Expressionism.

contexts.title: Moon Landing
contexts.description: Apollo 11 was the American spaceflight that first landed humans on the Moon. Commander Neil Armstrong and lunar module pilot Buzz Aldrin formed the American crew that landed the Apollo Lunar Module Eagle.

contexts.title: Bauhaus
contexts.description: German art school that combined crafts and fine arts, creating a revolutionary approach to design where form follows function.

contexts.title: Arts & Crafts Movement
contexts.description: An international movement that championed traditional craftsmanship against mass industrialization, favoring natural motifs and decorative honesty.

contexts.title: Mid-Century Modernism
contexts.description: Characterized by clean lines, organic shapes, and democratic mass-production materials like molded plywood, plastic, and fiberglass.
